title: How Harbourside Bike Hire works, and what is missing
question: How does Harbourside Bike Hire work today, and what is missing?
summary: A small Python prototype holds bikes by date and size and records returns. The documented web flow is not wired up here. Holds never expire, availability ignores bike status, and records disappear when the process stops. Proposed changes below are suggestions, not implemented features.

maps.title: How it works
maps.intro: Existing code and documented human steps, followed by a proposed working service.

journeys.title: Booking through return
journeys.summary: Follow the visitor, booking rules, records and staff handoffs.

steps.text: Choose a date and bike size
steps.detail: README describes a booking page. This checkout provides Python functions; no page, HTTP server or routing is present.

steps.text: Choose the first matching bike without a hold
steps.detail: book() calls hold_bike(); only size and the date/bike key are checked. STATUS is ignored.

steps.text: Keep the hold in process memory
steps.detail: The value is 15, not an expiration timestamp. No release mechanism exists.
Documented human step. No payment record is implemented.
check_out() delegates to mark_out(). Unknown identifiers and invalid transitions are accepted.

steps.text: Mark a bike as in; record damage on paper

steps.detail: No contact details or scheduler are present. The reported one-in-five rate is a staff estimate, not measured telemetry.

steps.text: Use a booking page with clear pickup terms
Reserve only a usable bike with an atomic check
Save bookings and expire abandoned holds
Allow staff to check out a valid booking
Report damage and block the bike until repaired
Send a reminder with customer permission

gaps.title: Holds never expire
gaps.why: As a visitor, I want abandoned holds released so I can book an available bike.

done_when: A hold has an expiry timestamp.
After 15 minutes an abandoned hold becomes available.
A confirmed booking survives temporary hold expiry.
stories.as: As a visitor, I want abandoned holds released so I can book an available bike.

gaps.title: Availability ignores bike condition and checkout state
gaps.why: As staff, I want only usable bikes offered so customers receive safe bikes.

done_when: An unavailable or damaged bike cannot be booked.
Concurrent requests cannot reserve the same bike for overlapping use.
Returning a damaged bike blocks future allocation until repair is recorded.
stories.as: As staff, I want only usable bikes offered so customers receive safe bikes.

gaps.title: Records disappear on restart
gaps.why: As staff, I want durable bookings so a restart does not lose reservations.

done_when: Bookings and bike state survive a process restart.
Reservation and status changes commit together or fail together.
stories.as: As staff, I want durable bookings so a restart does not lose reservations.

gaps.title: The documented web flow is not implemented
gaps.why: As a visitor or staff member, I want usable screens to complete the booking workflow.

done_when: A documented command starts the app from a fresh checkout.
A visitor can choose a date and size and see success or no availability.
Only authorized staff can change bike state.
Invalid dates, sizes, identifiers and state transitions are rejected.
stories.as: As a visitor or staff member, I want usable screens to complete the booking workflow.

gaps.title: No reminders or arrival tracking
gaps.why: As a visitor, I want a reminder so I remember my booking.

done_when: Pickup time and hold policy are defined before scheduling reminders.
Consenting customers receive one reminder at the agreed time.
Failed sends are visible to staff without duplicate delivery.
Arrival and no-show counts are measured; staff estimates remain labeled as estimates.
stories.as: As a visitor, I want a reminder so I remember my booking.

gaps.title: No automated tests or setup manifest
gaps.why: As a maintainer, I want repeatable checks so booking changes do not break availability.

done_when: Setup and launch dependencies are documented.
Checks cover expiry, persistence, concurrent allocation, damaged bikes and invalid staff actions.
stories.as: As a maintainer, I want repeatable checks so booking changes do not break availability.

notes.title: Booking terms
notes.body: The README says a day booking but the hold lasts 15 minutes in name only.
notes.recommend: Explain when the visitor must arrive.
notes.question: When should a reservation become a confirmed day booking?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Consistent records
notes.body: Separate dictionaries do not coordinate reservations and bike state.
notes.question: What overlapping hire periods must availability support?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Measure no-shows
notes.body: The one-in-five figure is a staff estimate for sunny Saturdays.
notes.recommend: Record arrivals and cancellations before comparing results.
notes.question: What will count as a no-show?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Build order
notes.body: Allocation currently ignores status and never releases holds.
notes.recommend: Fix allocation and expiry, then persistence and screens.
notes.question: Which booking failure should be covered first?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Prioritize damage handling
notes.body: Damage is recorded on paper and cannot block booking.
notes.question: Should damage blocking be the first release?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Staff access and contact data
notes.body: The functions have no authorization boundary; reminders would require contact data.
notes.recommend: Define staff access and collect only needed contact details.
notes.question: Who should be allowed to change bike condition?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Helpful reminders
notes.body: Staff want reminders the evening before.
notes.recommend: Agree useful reminder content with customers.
notes.question: What information would help customers arrive on time?
notes.author: Codex assistant

notes.title: Safe automation
notes.body: Expired holds could be released automatically once the policy is agreed.
notes.recommend: Automate expiry; leave repair clearance to staff.
notes.question: Which bike changes must always require a staff decision?
notes.author: Codex assistant

reading: Use Today and Side by side to compare the existing functions with the proposed workflow. Open boxes for code evidence; gaps contain user stories and completion checks. Role notes are assistant-authored review prompts.
